pairs.previous: I keep our drones and charging equipment in working order. My work includes adding new drones to the fleet, retiring old ones, setting up charging pads at our sites, and sending drones to charge. I also take drones out of service for repairs and put them back afterwards. Regulators can ask us to show how our drones have been looked after, and repairs and servicing are carried out by us technicians.

pairs.previous: I don't know about a specific worst day, but things that worry me include closures coming into force while drones of several companies are already in the air, closures being amended during the day, and batteries draining faster in cold and wind than planned. Radio coverage can be patchy around ports, industrial sites, and in bad weather, and reports from drones can arrive late, out of order, more than once, or not at all. Drones sometimes restart in flight after a software fault and carry on, and links used to give instructions to drones and charging equipment can send instructions twice while the sender cannot tell if the first attempt arrived.
pairs.question: With all those uncertainties you deal with, what do you check by hand today because you do not trust the system to do it?

pairs.previous: I am the licensed person responsible for each flight, and I decide which drone flies along which way, signing off a flight before it leaves. I can call off a flight, and while software never chooses a drone or a way for them, I do want help finding out which of my drones could get to where a job starts.
pairs.question: What are you afraid a new service would do wrong?

pairs.previous: I am worried because the platform company runs on a single server that is updated and restarted during working hours while drones are flying, and it occasionally crashes. We accept a few minutes of interruption, but closures can also come into force while drones of several companies are already in the air, and they are often amended during the day.
pairs.question: When something goes wrong during an operation, what do you need to know immediately?

pairs.previous: I keep the shared picture of the airspace by managing the network of flight corridors between sites, the zones grouping them, and the closures announced by the authorities. When a closure is entered, I want to know how much disruption it caused across customers. My work deals with planned closures with a start and end time, as well as sudden ones that apply at once, which are often amended during the day.
